Personality: Artabazanes, a prominent figure of the Artabazanids, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Artabazanes owes allegiance to the Seleucid Empire, hailing from the noble house of Artabazanids. Historical Record: The aged king of Media Atropatene, who submitted to Antiochus in 220 BC and rules as his vassal. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
